name: Calendar (Term-Structure) Arbitrage
summary: A genuine no-arbitrage violation: an American option expiring sooner trades above a same-strike option expiring later, so selling the near and buying the far locks a credit with a non-negative payoff.

legs.strike_rule: the NEAR expiry, at strike K where the violation is observed (works for puts identically)
the FAR expiry, SAME strike K

max_profit: The opening credit plus whatever value the far-dated option still carries after the near one expires
max_loss: Theoretically zero at the moment of entry, because an American option cannot be worth less than an identical option with more time. In practice: the cost of an early assignment on the near leg, plus financing and dividend effects, plus execution slippage.
breakevens: None - a correctly identified violation has no losing price region at the near expiry

greeks.delta: approximately zero at entry (same strike, similar deltas)
greeks.gamma: negative in the near, positive in the far
greeks.theta: positive while the near leg decays faster

when_to_use: Only when the scanner finds a real violation. On American options these appear around hard-to-borrow names, imminent special dividends, and stale quotes in illiquid chains - and they are usually a quote artifact rather than money. This entry exists so the system can tell the difference, sitting alongside the bank's vertical-strike and butterfly-convexity arbitrages as the third no-arbitrage check.
entry_rules: VIOLATION TEST, ON EXECUTABLE PRICES ONLY: near-expiry BID at strike K must exceed far-expiry ASK at the same strike and same right, by more than total round-trip costs. Mid prices do not count; a violation that disappears at the touch never existed.
Minimum edge: (near bid - far ask) x 100 >= $15 per contract after commissions, or skip it.
Quote freshness: both legs must have traded or updated within 60 seconds and both must show size >= 10 contracts.
Both legs same strike, same right, same underlying. Any strike or right mismatch makes this an ordinary calendar spread, not an arbitrage.

Dividend check: if an ex-dividend date falls between the two expiries, recompute - a large expected dividend legitimately makes the near call cheaper and the near put richer, and most apparent violations are exactly this.
Hard-to-borrow check: an elevated borrow rate can also explain the inversion legitimately; if the borrow rate exceeds 5% annualized, reject.
Submit as one MLeg order only. Never leg it - legging turns a riskless trade into a directional one.
management_rules: Hold to the near expiry, then decide on the far leg as a standalone position.
Close both legs immediately if the spread reverts to normal and the credit can be banked early with more than 50% of the edge captured.
If the near leg's short delta exceeds 0.80 before expiry, close the pair - the assignment risk now exceeds the arbitrage edge.
Never add size to a violation that persists; a persisting violation is almost always a data error.
exit_rules: ASSIGNMENT GUARD: the near leg is short and American; close it by 15:30 ET on its expiration day, always.
Close the near leg at extrinsic < $0.10 or |delta| >= 0.85, and before any ex-dividend date while a short call is ITM.
If the near leg is assigned, exercise or sell the far leg in the same session to flatten the resulting share position, and log it as an incident.
Never hold the far leg unhedged overnight after an unexpected assignment.
assignment_risk: The whole reason American term-structure violations exist. The short near leg can be assigned at any time, and on the deep-ITM side that is exactly when the counterparty will do it. An assignment converts a riskless credit into 100 shares that must be disposed of - which for this account is the failure mode, not the profit.
buying_power: Calendar spread requirement: with the long leg longer-dated at the same strike, brokers typically hold little to nothing beyond the net credit, but Alpaca's own calculation governs.
liquidity_needs: Both legs must be executable in one ticket at the quoted touch; this is where nearly all apparent violations die.
common_mistakes: Scanning on mids; ignoring dividends and borrow, which explain most inversions; legging in; treating a persistent violation as free money rather than as a broken feed.
zero_dte_notes: The near leg should never be 0DTE - the assignment window is too short to manage and the edge is always smaller than the pin risk.
family: Completeness gap-fill (cross-family): ratio/naked-financed put and call structures, quantity-unbalanced condors and strangles, stock+option overlays and monetizations, capital-protection and hybrid builds, 0DTE four-leg income, volatility-surface and relative-value trades, event-driven overlays, and roll/adjustment structures
